deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. Litt. E continues the reduction of the observations of the comet of 1772 (Montaigne's comet, later recognised as an apparition of Biela's comet). The previous page fixed the apparent obliquity, 23°28'2.83", and the Sun's place for observations 1 and 2. This page does three things: (A) the Sun's place for observation 3, (B) the Sun's place for observation 4, and (C) the apparent place for 1772 of the first comparison star, 5 (= gamma) Monocerotis. The next page continues with 7, 11 and an unnamed star in Monoceros, and then uses all of this to reduce the comet positions.

(A) SUN FOR OBSERVATION 3.
- Time. 1772 March 30, 8h39m59s (Paris apparent time) + 4m14.4s (equation of time, apparent to mean) + 33m35s (meridian difference Paris to Seeberg/Gotha, the meridian of von Zach's solar tables). This gives March 30, 9h17m48.4s Seeberg mean time.
- 9h17.80667m = 9.296777h, and 9.296777/24 = 0.387366 d, recorded as 'März 30.387366'.
- Mean longitude (signs of 30°). Epoch 1772 is 9s10°38'55.44". Add 2s27°43'21.39" for the day count; this is 89 days × 59'8.33", the tables counting the leap year one day short (my inference, consistent with the previous page). Add 22'54.48" for 9.2968h. The sum is 13s8°45'11.31", i.e. L = 8°45'11.31".
- Mean anomaly. It is carried in units of 1/10000 of the anomalistic year, counted from apogee: 5045.78 + 2436.61 + 10.62 = 7493.01, which is about 269.75° from apogee (about 89.75° from perigee).
- Perturbation arguments, in thousandths of the circle and summed mod 1000: (869,613,412,404) + (14,152,223,13) + (13,1,1,0) = (896,766,636,417).
- Equation of centre: 1°55'26.51" + 0.59" + 5.22" = 1°55'32.32".
- 8°45'11.31" + 1°55'32.32" = 10°40'43.63".
- Small corrections: -4.56 - 5.08 + 7.92 (planetary/lunar perturbation terms) and +28.96". The 28.96" is evidently a slowly varying constant; it becomes 28.86" four days later, a drift equal to that of the nutation in longitude. It is plausibly about +20" (removing the tabular aberration) plus about +9" (nutation); this decomposition is my conjecture.
- Result: Long. Sun = 10°41'10.89".
- Radius vector: 1.0002820 - 737 + 4 = 1.0002087; then +4 +291 -185 -97 gives R = 1.0002100, log R = 0.0000912.

(B) SUN FOR OBSERVATION 4.
- Time. April 3, 8h57m21s + 3m1.5s + 33m35s = 9h33m57.5s. That is 33.958333m, 9.565972h, and 0.398582 d, written as 'März 34.398582'.
- Mean longitude: 9s10°38'55.44" + 3s1°39'54.71" + 23'34.28" gives 12°42'24.43".
- Anomaly: 5045.78 + 2546.12 + 10.93 = 7602.83.
- Arguments: (032,773,646,418).
- Equation of centre: 1°55'2.46" + 5.21" = 1°55'7.67", giving 14°37'32.10".
- Corrections +1.50 - 4.47 + 8.14 + 28.86 give Long. Sun = 14°38'6.15".
- Radius vector: 1.0013351 + 297 + 12 = 1.0013660, then +359 -188 -79 gives 1.0013752, log = 0.0005968.

(C) STAR 5 MONOCEROTIS.
- Catalogue place for 1800: alpha = 91°16'29.1" (the arithmetic requires .1), delta = -6°13'24.2". The epoch of observation is 1772.229, and 1800 - 1772.229 = 27.771 years (log 1.44359).
- Precession is computed with the mean place alpha = 91°5'36", delta = -6°13'.4.
  - Annual precession in RA: m + n sin(alpha) tan(delta), with m = 45.8817" and log n = 1.30116 (n = 20.006").
  - log n + log sin(alpha) + log tan|delta| = 1.30116 + 9.99992 + 9.03752 = 0.33860, giving 2.1807". This term is negative because delta < 0.
  - So the annual RA precession is 45.8817 - 2.1807 = 43.701" (log 1.64049), and 43.701 × 27.771 = 1213.6" = 20'13.6".
  - Annual precession in declination: n cos(alpha), with log 1.30116 + 8.28061 = 9.58177, giving -0.3817"/yr. Over 27.771 yr this is 10.6".
- Mean place 1772: alpha = 91°16'29.1" - 20'13.61" = 90°56'15.49"; delta = -6°13'24.2" + 10.6" = -6°13'13.60".
- Aberration, in the h, H, i form, with Sun = 7°13' (the mean of the solar longitudes 6°43' and 7°42' of observations 1 and 2) and aberration constant 20":
  - h = 20 sqrt(cos²(Sun) cos²(eps) + sin²(Sun)) = 18.37", log 1.2641 (negative).
  - tan H = cos(Sun) cos(eps)/sin(Sun), so H = 82°8' and H + alpha = 173°4'.
  - RA: h sin(H+alpha) sec(delta): 1.2641n + 9.0807 + 0.0026 = 0.3474n, giving -2.23".
  - Dec: h cos(H+alpha) sin(delta): 1.2641n + 9.9968n + 9.0348n = 0.2957n, giving -1.976".
  - Constant dec term: i cos(delta) = -20 sin(eps) cos(Sun) cos(delta) = -7.85". It is apparently evaluated by the product-to-sum rule as -10 sin(eps)[cos(Sun+delta) + cos(Sun-delta)] = -3.98" - 3.87". This fits the present page to 0.01"; it fits the next page's stars less well.
- Nutation. Node at 7s0°15' = 210°15'.
  - Common RA term: delta_psi cos(eps) = -18" sin(Omega) cos(eps) = +8.32".
  - Variable part in the form B, G with G = Omega - 6°36' = 203°39', so G - alpha = 112°43'.
  - B = -sqrt((delta_psi sin eps)² + (delta_eps)²) = -9.006" (log 0.9545n). This implies delta_psi = 9.07" (coefficient 18") and delta_eps = -8.25" (coefficient about 9.55"); this is my inference.
  - RA: B cos(G-alpha) tan(delta): 0.9545n + 9.5868n + 9.0374n = 9.5787n, giving -0.379".
  - Dec: B sin(G-alpha): 0.9545n + 9.9649 = 0.9194n, giving -8.31".
- Apparent place:
  - alpha = 90°56'15.49" - 2.23 - 0.38 + 8.32 = 90°56'21.20".
  - delta = -6°13'13.60" - 1.976 - 3.98 - 3.87 - 8.31 = -6°13'31.73" (written 31.72).
- These apparent star places, together with the solar longitudes and log R, feed the comet reductions on the next page. The whole page is standard 'Reduction' work of the kind described in Gauss's 1805 orbit computations.
errors: All four solar longitudes in this sequence (including the two on the previous page) come out 0.02" larger than the written partial sums. Here 10°40'43.63" + 27.24" = 10°41'10.87" (written 10.89), and 14°37'32.10" + 34.03" = 14°38'6.13" (written 6.15). This suggests either an unwritten +0.02" term or a constant actually 28.98"; it is negligible.

The declination aberration term computed from the logs is 10^0.2957 = 1.976", but the entry reads 1,967 (a transposition, by Gauss or in the reading). The final declination should then be -6°13'31.73" rather than 31.72"; the 0.01" difference is negligible.
The leading RA digits must be 91°16'29.1" (not 29.8") for 91°16'29.1" - 20'13.61" = 90°56'15.49" to hold. Gauss overwrote the figure.
No substantive errors. All log computations checked (precession 1213.6", 10.6"; aberration -2.23"; nutation -0.38", -8.31"; log R values) are correct to the last place shown.

results.what: Reduction of Paris apparent times of Messier's 1772 comet observations to Seeberg (Gotha) mean time, using the equation of time and a 33m35s meridian difference, and expression as decimal days.
results.modern_name: Time reduction (apparent to mean solar time, change of meridian)

results.what: Solar longitude and radius vector from von Zach's solar tables. Mean longitude, anomaly in 1/10000 year, equation of centre, perturbation arguments, and constant aberration/nutation correction.
results.modern_name: Computation of solar ephemeris from tables (Zach, Tabulae motuum Solis 1792)

results.what: Precession of a star from catalogue epoch 1800 to 1772.229, using annual precession in RA m + n sin(alpha) tan(delta) and in declination n cos(alpha), evaluated at the mean place.
results.modern_name: Annual precession formulas in right ascension and declination

results.what: Reduction to apparent place. Aberration in the form h sin(H+alpha) sec(delta), h cos(H+alpha) sin(delta) + i cos(delta); nutation as a common RA term plus B cos(G-alpha) tan(delta), B sin(G-alpha); computed logarithmically. Coefficients: aberration 20", nutation about 18" and about 9.55".
results.modern_name: Star-dependent/day-dependent factorisation of aberration and nutation (precursor of Besselian day numbers)
results.usually_credited_to: Lalande, Zach (Tabulae aberrationis et nutationis 1806); later systematised by Bessel (1830)

results.what: Orbit reductions for the comet of 1772 in 1805, in connection with its identification with the comet of 1805.
results.modern_name: Recognition of the 1772/1805 comet identity (later Biela's comet)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Olbers and Bessel (1805-06); periodicity established 1826 by Biela, Gambart and Clausen

deep.surprise_reason: Purely routine positional-astronomy reductions (solar tables, precession, aberration, nutation) preparing observations of the comet of 1772 for orbit determination. Gauss's involvement with the 1772/1805 comet is documented, and nothing methodologically new appears.

checkable.asserts: Day term 2s27°43'21.39" equals 89 days of mean solar motion 59'8.33"/day.
Hourly term 22'54.48" equals mean motion over 9.296777 h.
Keplerian solar distance near true anomaly 91.6° agrees with Gauss's R = 1.00021.
Declination precession over 27.771 years equals -10.6" (applied with sign to give +10.6").
Aberration amplitude h for Sun = 7°13' is 18.37" (log 1.2641).
H + alpha = 173°4', whose log sin is 9.0807.
The two declination terms 3.98" + 3.87" equal 20" sin(eps) cos(Sun) cos(delta).
Nutation in RA (common part) equals +8.32" with node at 210°15' and coefficient 18".
Nutation amplitude B = 9.006" (log 0.9545) with coefficients 18" and 9.55".

transcription_corrections: '20 13,61' is the subtracted precession -20'13",61, not a separate quantity.
'@7.13' is Sun = 7°13' (the sun symbol), the solar longitude used for aberration.
'+ 3 1,5[?]' is +3'1",5 (equation of time), confirmed by the sum 9h33'57",5.
'1,967' in the declination column is probably 1,976 (the value from log 0.2957).
'− 6. 13. 4' near the top right is -6°13'.4 (mean declination used in the precession logs); '91. 5. 36' is the mean RA 91°5'36".
In the third Sun section, '1,0002087 +4' is the subtotal 1.0002087 followed by a further +4 correction.
